answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and put them face down on the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; unused Conflict cards returned without looking.

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their garrison, nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, player components: score on 1 in 4P, otherwise 0; two Agents; three garrison troops and remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn with Agents remaining. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the cards still in your hand that you reveal, not from cards already played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns optional; after Reveal your turns are skipped. Reveal steps resolve just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: You cannot use the played Agent card's effects or destination effects to pay that same visit's entry cost: the cost is paid immediately before resolving either. A legal Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can grant resources that are available to pay the entry cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs immediately before resolving space/card effects; one card can't send multiple Agents; card with no Agent icons only revealed. Plot resources gained before entry can pay.

answers.answer: You may deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for five total. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy units. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison; the Combat-space rule permits deploying this turn's recruits plus up to two from garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruits from supply to garrison; at Combat space deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you already have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a post connected to the occupied space to ignore another player's Agent and send your Agent there. Gather Intelligence recalls your Spy from a connected post when you place an Agent, to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before any space or played-card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both effects; you may use two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; Gather Intelligence timing is immediately after placing Agent; same Spy cannot be recalled for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot play Combat Intrigue because eligibility requires at least one deployed unit.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; if last unit removed strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: may play or pass; passing earlier doesn't bar later play; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply and worms to bank; markers reset.

answers.answer: In either four- or three-player play, two tied for first each receive the second-place reward, neither wins, and nobody takes the Conflict card. In four-player play the remaining players compete for the third reward; in three-player play no other reward is given. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in 4P leaves others competing for third; tie first in 3 or fewer gives no other rewards; no winner/card; zero strength gets none.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, the doubled reward lets you pay the cost a second time: pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice total for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: if one or more worms, double rewards; control and battle icons excluded; may pay cost a second time (3 spice for 1 VP, or 6 for 2).

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A matching battle icon must be matched: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, also for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Winner first takes card face up, then checks mandatory battle-icon pair; cards qualify if face-up Conflict or Objective; Endgame wild matches any one.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose that VP below 2 and regain it upon reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence falls below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which stays only while holding the token. Tying the holder does not steal it: a challenger must rise above them (or the separate FAQ holder-loss trigger can transfer it).
answers.evidence: Faction Influence scoring: 2 VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus retained; Alliance tied to holder, ties don't steal; rising above transfers.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, you may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split a source across multiple cards. The Row refills immediately to five, so you may buy a replacement during the same Reveal if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion usable before/between/after Reveal effects; pool or split; Row always five; acquired card face up in discard.

answers.answer: At each Agent-free Maker space (Deep Desert, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin), add 1 bank spice to its bonus-spice spot in Makers; visiting gains all accumulated bonus spice, including when choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. The Shield Wall prevents worm summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery and Imperial Basin until removed. Worms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never in a garrison. Maker Hooks are required only when specified by the effect and are retained, not spent; a summoning effect without that requirement does not need Hooks.
answers.evidence: Makers adds spice to empty spaces. Board Space Guide lists costs/base/worm choices. Sandworms: Shield Wall protected locations; never garrison; Hooks not universal and never spent.

answers.answer: At Recall, after the round's phases, 10 or more VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. The listed resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Game end: end of round; Endgame Intrigue then most VP; tiebreakers spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup shuffles the 20 standard contract tokens face down, exposes two face up, and leaves 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The ten contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left in the box, not included in this setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Components says 20 standard tokens and contrasting backs only with Rise of Ix.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and available contracts, a contract icon takes one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and flips a replacement from the bank face up. If all contracts have been taken by players, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest is completed by visiting a Maker space and gaining the listed amount of spice that turn in total from all sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts sections state icon replacement/fallback and each completion trigger.

answers.answer: No. A board-space contract taken after you already sent an Agent to that space this turn must wait until a future turn, because you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave the token in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must have had contract at time Agent sent; completed contract announced, rewards gained, flipped face down and left in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; First Player is the human whose dealt Objective shows the First Player marker, and First Player alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: one Rival, Ornithopter Objective, First Player among humans; Rival immediately clockwise; never takes Reveal turn.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: it tries an empty post of the specified type, ignores placement if none exists, and immediately reveals another card to continue the Agent turn. The Rival ignores ordinary space costs and effects and applies only Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination; Place Spy cards do not place Agent; ignore normal costs/effects; empty deck or Reshuffle immediately reshuffle.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing any whose 1–3P or 4/6P marking does not match the player count, then distribute one random Objective face up to each player; the Objective showing the First Player marker determines First Player. Shaddam may not be chosen without the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objectives, shuffle, distribute one face up; Shaddam not used unless playing CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank's Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; substitute conveniently if they run out. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments go back to it.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: resources/sandworms not meant to be limited; make substitution. Gains from bank and payments returned. Recruiting: empty troop supply prevents recruitment.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the top Conflict card and place it face up on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds, resolve control defense, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists phases; Round Start reveals Conflict before drawing five; Recall describes next-round preparation.

answers.answer: Yes. Space effects, the Agent-box effects and the Faction Influence advance may be carried out in any order. No, the visit's Influence cannot pay its entry requirement: costs and requirements must be met before placement and before resolving effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: effects in any order; must pay costs and meet requirements immediately before resolving space/card effects.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect may normally be paid only once per turn, so not twice; the exception is doubling a Conflict reward with sandworms. Most card and space effects are mandatory, except effects marked “may,” optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play the Intrigue; an Intrigue still requires paying all its costs. A direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory.
answers.evidence: Arrows: once per turn except doubled rewards. FAQ mandatory effects and costs lists exceptions and Intrigue costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spy in supply when one must be placed, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies a connected Agent-icon type, the post must connect to that type or you cannot place it.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post; may recall a Spy for no effect if supply empty; some effects specify Agent icon required.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate only bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. You cannot recall a Spy without playing a card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement; you may recall two for different effects, one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; recall requires an Agent turn card (FAQ); two spies can serve different effects but not two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller receives the listed bonus whenever anyone visits, including when the controller is the visitor: Arrakeen and Spice Refinery give the controller 1 Solari; Imperial Basin gives 1 spice. Winning the corresponding Conflict places or transfers the Control marker, replacing an opponent's marker. When the Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to it, without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control describes bonuses, marker transfer and defensive troop from supply when Conflict revealed.

answers.answer: A tie for second gives each tied player the third-place reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. A tie for third gives those tied players nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody wins or takes the card, and there are no other rewards even in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Combat tie rules and explicit three-tied-for-first note.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards and third receives nothing. This also applies in two-player play with the Rival as the third competitor; ordinary first and second rewards are paid, and ordinary third is paid only in a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 2–3 players first and second rewards; third only in tie for second; Rival counts as third competitor.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues can be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolution place them face up in the discard pile beside the Intrigue Deck. If that deck runs out, shuffle its discard to make a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section gives timing, storage/discard; FAQ says reshuffle Intrigue discard when deck runs out.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless the instruction specifies Intrigue. It discards a card of your choice from your hand, not from in play or the discard pile. Secrets steals one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding and Intrigue sections; Steal Intrigue icon specifies opponents with 4+ and random selection.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play, removing them from the game; ordinary cards return to the box and Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP is retained if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; Victory FAQ says Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained after trashing.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire that card, not when you later play it. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to discard.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond section.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed this turn; it may be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ confirms retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain-two-Influence effect selects one Faction, so the two Influence cannot be split across different Factions. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its specified threshold with the named Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free choice gain two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the formerly tied opponents are eligible; with several tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ Alliance loss: formerly tied player takes it; if several tied, former holder chooses; return to board if nobody 4+.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect remains face up until that effect applies, then is used and discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because no one wins. If you receive it as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: winning-Conflict Intrigues cannot be played after tie; if received as winning reward may be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: Victory FAQ: if resource tiebreakers tied, most recent Reveal wins; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with that one Agent placement. The contract must have been held when the Agent was sent. Its completion is another effect of the Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all held contracts for same space with one placement; board-space contract is another effect, resolve in any order.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the two set-aside Sardaukar contracts. When acquiring a contract, he may choose one of those instead of a generally available contract; no other player may acquire them. His Signet Ring deployment restriction begins immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM reserved contracts; Shaddam FAQ says restriction immediate and lasts only that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of the Training track and stays at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2, and reaching 2 can happen again later after losing Influence and regaining it. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications for Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, is not a Faction, and always draws one card; its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM, takes an available contract with CHOAM, and reverts to 2 Solari if none remain. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, gives 1 Emperor Influence once (automatic as a Faction space and listed effect are the same gain), plus the same contract-icon effect. Thus only Dutiful Service automatically advances a Faction track.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide intro says Accept Contract is non-Faction and Dutiful Service is Emperor; shared contract-icon rule and table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller separately gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert uses Spice Trade and costs 3 water; base choice is 4 spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin uses Spice Trade and costs 1 water; base choice is 2 spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon one worm. In either space you gain all accumulated bonus spice even when choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Deep Desert/Hagga Basin rows; Maker spaces award all bonus spice; Hooks are never spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row and introduction.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, is not a Combat space, and costs 5 Solari each visit. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On later visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster, then 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may visit only once per game. The third Agent becomes available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Its effects allow discarding an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recalling one of your other Agents and drawing a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence and cannot recall the Agent just sent this turn.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; Recall Agent rule says other Agent, not this turn's Agent.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops either way, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is Combat: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice, gaining 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari if paid; its controller also receives 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild icon, Combat yes, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen icon, Combat yes, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and may trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor icon, Combat no, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad, costs nothing, and is not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, is not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild, costs nothing, is not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders moves each affected opponent's Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected to that destination. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Manipulate prevents opponents from acquiring the removed card. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water; its Score and Combat markers are 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10 VP triggers Endgame at Recall like a human's, and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup and two-player game description.

answers.answer: As soon as total eligible resources reach the Rival's printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many and takes its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together, one each. Spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue, water; keep leftovers. The resource rule applies as soon as the threshold is reached.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends a set of 7 Solari for 1 VP, or 7 spice for 1 VP, or 3 Intrigue cards for 1 VP, or 3 water for 1 VP. It does not spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP; these are separate exact sets.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival selects the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by the leftmost icon in its priority list. It gains Influence VP and Alliances like a human, including VP at 2 and Alliance VP, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival resources/scoring and Combat sections; numbered Influence icon explanation.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination Hagal card, choose only the destination matching the current condition; if it is occupied, reveal another Hagal card without using the other destination. The choices are selected by Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns gives conditions and says if selected destination occupied, reveal new card without other destination.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none; newly recruited troops are also deployed there. At noncombat spaces, recruited troops go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus that it does not meet does not prevent Agent placement; apply only the eligible Hagal effects.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: at every Combat space deploy up to two from garrison; conditional bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival visits a Combat space on that same turn, those newly recruited troops can deploy there too. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes: Scheme recruits before Agent placement deploy; Place Spy always reveals another card.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects all accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of taking base spice; without Hooks, or if worms are prohibited, it takes base spice instead (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert). Hooks are required for these Rival worm choices. The bonus spice is collected regardless.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: always collects all bonus spice; Hooks and Conflict permissions determine worm choice; if none summoned take base spice.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to its strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window, so they can respond afterward. A unit-free Rival gets no Hagal strength bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes: the Rival can gain control bonuses on visits, deploy its defensive troop from supply when a controlled location's Conflict is revealed, win cards and battle-icon VP normally, and double rewards with sandworms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; even with CHOAM a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: During Reveal effect resolution, total and announce Combat strength and set the marker at any point; it can be updated as needed during the turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start counting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength sections.

answers.answer: A Leader's second ability, marked by the Signet Ring icon, activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns. Merely revealing Signet Ring does not activate it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities and Overview card rule.

answers.answer: The Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects that may be done by recalling a Spy without a card.
answers.evidence: Spies section distinguishes Recall Spy icon from the two no-card recall effects.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing and Discarding sections.

answers.answer: A sandworm-doubled reward of one Influence of your choice can be taken twice, and the two instances may be with the same Faction or two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect that grants two free-choice Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Sandworm example permits same or two different Factions; Influence section says gain-two free choice can't choose two factions.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring effect shown on the Rival's Hagal card as directed by its printed Signet Ring ability. It is a Hagal effect and does not require a human Signet Ring card or a Rival Reveal turn; the Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; it never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon takes a token from the bank if the Rival lacks Hooks; if it already has one, it takes none. A Shield Wall removal icon removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks or if the Wall is already gone, ignore it with no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues then gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. Visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice. Its controller gets 1 spice; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player receives both the visit's spice and controller bonus.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; intro says resolve visitor and controller bonuses even if same player.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from previous rounds. Then resolve any defensive troop bonus and each player draws five cards; the Conflict is revealed before the draws.
answers.evidence: Round Start phase description.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. The four Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of those tracks, so no player begins holding one. The Shield Wall token begins in its marked area below Spice Refinery; it is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the First Player takes the first turn and play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of Player Turns; that phase ends once all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, priority starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise; an eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass. Passing does not prevent acting later, and the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat Intrigue sections.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are: reveal all remaining hand cards face up; resolve Reveal-box effects of those just-revealed cards and use Persuasion/acquire cards while resolving; Clean Up by moving all cards in front of you to discard. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps; effects gained in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place face down in their supply. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards, shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal five Imperium cards face up to the Row, and put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; their three Spies and Councilor start in supply; Control markers also start in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states; per-player component placement.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, you may acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is at the card's top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during Reveal, not Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards section.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal placement or recall exists. A Shield Wall detonation icon says you may remove it, so removal is optional. Once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: placement/recall optional; Shield Wall section says may remove, gone rest of game.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon, unless the card has the Spy Agent icon and you have a Spy at a post connected to that destination. A Spy connected to Shipping does not grant access to a card showing only City. If the card actually has the Spy Agent icon, that connected Spy allows access without recalling it.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy Agent icon rules.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before Agent placement are available to pay the entry cost. Resources from the Agent card or destination occur after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placing Agent; pre-entry gains can pay; destination/card gains after placement cannot.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Player Turns ends and Combat begins only after both humans Revealed and the Rival used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule.

answers.answer: At Round Start, when a Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit; taking the bonus is optional. After Combat rewards, reset all Combat markers to 0 before the Makers phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start control defense and Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you, then send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve that played card's Agent box, ignoring its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or take one from your discard pile for this Agent turn, and cannot simply move an Agent already on the board; send an Agent from your Leader (or recall another via a specific effect).
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand, send Agent from Leader, resolve Agent box. Recall Agent is a separate effect.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent. He cannot delay its start by resolving board-space effects first; it prevents deploying units for that entire turn.
answers.evidence: Shaddam clarification: restriction takes effect immediately; general freedom to order effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no sandworms, first, second and third receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth receives no reward. The first-place player wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 4P first, second, third receive rewards; player with highest strength wins and takes card; zero strength gets none.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards section: own deck, reshuffle when empty; not a chosen discard card.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A player who acquires one moves it from the bank onto their garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: all 4 Hooks in common bank; later acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust the participant's Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The adjusted strength shown on the track is used for Combat rewards; the Reveal value is not fixed for the whole round.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: adjust marker when card resolves; total set during Reveal not fixed for rest of round.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice and water come from the common bank. They are not taken from another player's supply. Payments of those resources are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: whenever gain take from bank; whenever pay return resources to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down before exposing two face-up offers; put all remaining tokens face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the face-down order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle remaining tokens face down, flip two face up, rest face down in bank.

answers.answer: Before the contract shuffle, set aside both Sardaukar contracts from the 20 standard contracts. Only Shaddam can acquire them, and setting them aside does not give them to him. Shuffle the other 18, expose two as public offers, and put the remaining 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
